title: Week 8 MFPI analysis: Tupelo High School leads the statewide rankings
dek: What moved in the Week 8 Mississippi Football Power Index, computed from verified results through Oct 20.
author: MFPI automated analysis

sources.label: MHSAA official score center (schedules and scores)
Statewide media rankings used for the Media Rank inputs

limitations: Generated from the published snapshot; no games after the cutoff are included.
Media Rank and Media Strength of Schedule contribute 20% of every rating; MFPI's own score-based model contributes 80%.
No player, injury, coaching or game-narrative information is used or implied.

sections.heading: The top of the statewide rankings
paragraphs: [[tupelo]] (8-0) is No. 1 for the 8th straight published week. MFPI rating: increased 0.4 points to 97.1. In the latest window it beat [[hernando]] (currently No. 19) 42-7 at home on Oct 15.
No. 2 [[gulfport]] (6-1, 7A): ranking up 1 spot to No. 2 (from No. 3); rating increased 1.3 points to 95.2. It beat [[west-harrison]] (currently No. 57) 47-6 at home on Oct 16.
No. 3 [[warren-central]] (7-0, 6A): ranking down 1 spot to No. 3 (from No. 2); rating decreased 0.2 points to 94.3. It beat [[greenville]] (currently No. 100) 45-6 at home on Oct 16.
No. 4 [[diberville]] (8-0, 7A): ranking unchanged at No. 4; rating increased 0.5 points to 93.2. It beat [[st-martin]] (currently No. 18) 55-50 at home on Oct 16.
No. 5 [[starkville]] (5-2, 7A): ranking up 3 spots to No. 5 (from No. 8); rating increased 1.0 points to 91.3. It beat [[clinton]] (currently No. 35) 31-17 on the road on Oct 16.

sections.heading: Classification leaders
paragraphs: Class ranks are the statewide order filtered to one classification; MFPI never recalculates a separate class rating.
Every classification kept the same No. 1 team as the previous week.

sections.heading: Results that raised ratings most
paragraphs: The largest rating increases among teams with a verified result in this window. A rating can also move without a game, because every opponent's rating is re-solved each week.
[[biloxi]] (+9.3 to 61.7, now No. 78) beat [[harrison-central]] (currently No. 112) 30-14 on the road on Oct 16.
[[lewisburg]] (+7.7 to 58.4, now No. 92) beat [[southaven]] (currently No. 85) 28-7 at home on Oct 16.
[[magee]] (+7.0 to 63.2, now No. 74) beat [[raleigh]] (currently No. 52) 29-7 at home on Oct 16.
[[franklin]] (+6.4 to 47.6, now No. 118) beat [[hazlehurst]] (currently No. 77) 35-34 on the road on Oct 16.
[[purvis]] (+6.1 to 44.7, now No. 125) beat [[stone]] (currently No. 106) 21-14 at home on Oct 16.
The full list of movers is in the [[risers-and-fallers:2026-week-08-risers-and-fallers]] analysis.

sections.heading: Schedule strength
paragraphs: MFPI strength of schedule is the average current rating of every completed opponent, expressed as a statewide percentile (100 is the strongest schedule in this week's field, not a perfect grade). The five strongest schedules: [[west-point]] (0-7, SOS percentile 100.0); [[oxford]] (6-1, SOS percentile 99.6); [[germantown]] (4-4, SOS percentile 99.1); [[brandon]] (5-2, SOS percentile 98.7); [[starkville]] (5-2, SOS percentile 98.2).

Teams that have played furthest above their own classification (average class steps up, games up in class): [[okolona]] (1A, +1.83, 5 up); [[byers]] (1A, +1.60, 4 up); [[charleston]] (2A, +1.50, 5 up); [[poplarville]] (4A, +1.43, 5 up); [[laurel]] (5A, +1.33, 5 up).

sections.heading: Data notes and limitations
paragraphs: Snapshot generated October 20, 2026 at 11:20 AM Central with a cutoff of October 20 at 11:00 AM Central, formula MFPI-3.2.
871 of 892 game listings due by the cutoff had verified scores (97.7%); the rest count as unavailable, never as losses or 0-0 results.
Opponent ranks in this article are the opponent's rank in this snapshot, not its rank on the day the game was played, unless a sentence says otherwise.
